column7: #3041 review: after a session token validated, the HTTP auth middleware re-read the session row for its setup-only flag (and, in separate reads, its impersonator and expiry) and on a failed read served the request with SetupOnly=false, no impersonator and no expiry clamp, and cached that identity. A setup-only session whose revocation had not landed (or failed) then had full API access the moment the store faltered and kept it from the cache after the store recovered. Now one read, core.ResolveSessionAuthFacts, supplies every per-session fact; a failed read refuses the request with 503 (nothing cached, no brute-force strike) and is logged and audited as auth.session_facts_unavailable. EndSetupSessionIfComplete no longer discards a failed revocation: its completion event says the sessions could not be revoked. Red before: 200 with the store faulted, 200 again from the cache after it recovered, no audit row.
